clue.text: Gershwin found it fascinating

parts.note: a nod to the title of the Gershwin brothers' song 'Fascinating ...', so the thing they called fascinating is the song's subject

explanation.walkthrough: The Gershwins wrote the 1924 song 'Fascinating Rhythm'; the clue asks what they found fascinating.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title pairs the adjective with a musical beat or pulse, so that beat is what Gershwin found fascinating.

clue.text: Holder of unorthodox opinion about master of alchemy

indicators.note: about means the dissenter goes around the master

parts.note: a heretic holds unorthodox views
M is short for master, as in MA, Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A dissenter has views about a master alchemist.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside HERETIC after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermetic derives from Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy, and means relating to the occult sciences.

clue.text: Entry made by soldiers after gin party

indicators.note: after places the soldiers at the end, following the other pieces

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap
a do is a party
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers make their entrance after a gin party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is a snare, not the drink; 'made by' simply links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapdoor is a hinged opening in a floor or ceiling, a way in.

clue.text: Take medicine initially to get rid of pain from this growth

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word medicine

parts.note: to oust is to get rid of
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Advice to take medicine to relieve the pain of a growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growth' sounds medical, but it is hair on the upper lip.
explanation.definitionFit: A moustache is hair grown on the upper lip, a facial growth.

clue.text: Carriage mostly fetched before midday

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word for fetched is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: fetched means brought
AM, ante meridiem, means before midday

explanation.surface: A carriage was brought round to someone's door some time in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final T of BROUGHT, leaving BROUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A brougham is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn closed carriage of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Drink best ale set out for enjoyment

indicators.note: out means the letters of the preceding words are put out of order

explanation.surface: Beer is set out at a party for everyone's enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: All four words, Drink included, are the fodder; 'set' is part of it, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer and skittles is an idiom for pleasure and amusement, as in 'life isn't all...'.

clue.text: Idealistic Scotsman supporting university chief

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts the Scotsman underneath the other pieces

parts.note: top means chief or leading
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: An idealistic Scot backs the head of a university.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'supporting' means placed below.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian comes from More's 'Utopia', an ideal state, so it means aiming at an impossibly perfect world.

clue.text: Crown wheels for the pit-head hoist

definitions.meaning: a crown is something worn on the head
in mining, the winding wheels on the frame above a pit shaft

explanation.surface: A crown wheel is used on a colliery lift.
explanation.definitionFit: Headgear means anything worn on the head, and is also the mining term for the hoisting frame and pulleys over a shaft.

clue.text: A creature found in many a wood

indicators.note: found in means the creature is placed within the word for many

parts.note: a hog is a creature, a pig

explanation.surface: A creature lurks in many a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many a wood' reads as a phrase, but MANY is the container and 'a' is the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a hard reddish-brown tropical timber.

clue.text: The sweetheart sought by Squire Trelawney?

definitions.meaning: a darling or beloved person, as in calling someone 'my precious'
Squire Trelawney funds the voyage to the island in Stevenson's novel, hunting buried gold

explanation.surface: A romantic hero goes looking for his beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: Squire Trelawney is a character in Robert Louis Stevenson's 'Treasure Island', who sets out after Flint's hoard.
explanation.definitionFit: A beloved person can be called a treasure; the squire's quest in the novel is for buried gold, a hoard of valuables.

clue.text: Tree shoot first used in making soap

indicators.note: first says the shoot word comes before the tree word in the answer

parts.note: to shoot is to pot, as with a gun at game
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Instructions for soap-making that begin with a tree shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the shoot (POT) ahead of the tree (ASH), reversing the clue's order. 'Shoot' as a verb, to pot game, not a sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash, potassium carbonate from wood ashes, was the traditional alkali for making soft soap.

clue.text: Surgeon volunteers to encompass conclusion of feud

indicators.note: to encompass means the surgeon and volunteers wrap around the conclusion

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
a conclusion is an end
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A surgeon calls in volunteers to bring a long feud to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusion of feud' looks like 'last letter of feud' (D), but 'conclusion' is END and 'feud' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter feud, originally a blood feud between families.

clue.text: Flirt originally found in Zola's carriage

indicators.note: originally signals the opening letters of the next three words

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled carriage

explanation.surface: A flirtatious woman is first spotted riding in the novelist Zola's carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' seems to go with Flirt, but it governs 'found in Zola's', giving F, I, Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizgig is an old word for a frivolous, flighty girl, a coquette.

clue.text: Sea creature a girl introduced to an islander

indicators.note: introduced to means the girl comes in front of the following word

parts.note: an orc is a killer whale or similar sea monster
Di is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A sea creature and a girl are presented to someone from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Orcadians come from Orkney, the islands off northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: An Orcadian is a native of Orkney, an archipelago, so an inhabitant of islands.

clue.text: Visit a cat made, reverting to primitive type

indicators.note: made means the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A visiting cat turns wild again.
explanation.definitionFit: Atavistic describes a throwback to ancestral characteristics.

clue.text: Colourful, but not allowed to make a mark

indicators.note: but not says the following piece is taken away from what precedes

parts.note: scarlet is a bright, colourful red
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Something is bright but forbidden to leave a trace.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARLET loses LET, leaving the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin by a healed wound.

clue.text: Impressive advance in the lifting of depressions

indicators.note: in places the advance inside the depressions
in a down entry the lifting of a word reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: dips are depressions in the ground
to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: An impressive rise follows an economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the lifting of' turns DIPS upward to read SPID, since this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid means magnificent, grand, striking.

clue.text: Wood used to build vessel featured in book

indicators.note: featured in places the vessel inside the book

parts.note: an album is a book of photos or stamps
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Timber used to make a pot appears in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Alburnum is sapwood, the soft young wood beneath a tree's bark.

clue.text: Girl embracing royal host

indicators.note: embracing means the girl's name wraps around the royal letter

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
R stands for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A girl hugs a royal host at a reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' is a multitude, not a party-giver.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great multitude, especially of soldiers, as in 'the heavenly host'.

clue.text: Admin officer's son leaves to adapt a series of books

indicators.note: leaves means the letter for son departs the word

parts.note: to adjust is to adapt
NT is the New Testament, a series of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An administrator's son quits to adapt a book series.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the S from ADJUST leaves ADJUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjutant is the staff officer who handles a unit's administration.

clue.text: Publication in one eastern state, unknown in another

indicators.note: in puts the eastern state and the unknown together inside the other state

parts.note: Maine is a US state
GA is Georgia, on the US east coast
Z is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A periodical appears in one eastern US state and is unknown in another.
explanation.walkthrough: Both US states are given by their postal abbreviations or full names; the second 'in' just repeats the sense of placing within.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine is a periodical publication.

clue.text: Two sets of cards employed on board

parts.note: a deck is a full pack of cards
a hand is the set of cards dealt to one player

explanation.surface: Two packs of cards are used in a game played on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' is a ship, as in 'on board'; the deck and hand are two different card sets.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is a sailor working on a ship's deck, a member of the crew aboard.

clue.text: Debt-collector, for example, upset about imprisonment here

parts.note: a dun is one who demands payment of debts

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the abbreviation for example upside down

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A debt collector is distressed about being locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark underground cell, a place of confinement.

clue.text: Like an Arab — one of several in the extremities of Europe

indicators.note: in says the piece sits inside the outer letters
the extremities of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together

explanation.surface: An Arab stands out as one of many in the far ends of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' is a horse breed, not a person: the first and last letters of Europe, E and E, enclose QUIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab is a breed of horse, so it is horse-like by nature.

clue.text: Board conducting a judicial examination involving food

indicators.note: involving means the examination wraps around the food

parts.note: a trial is a judicial examination in court
a bun is a piece of food

explanation.surface: A panel conducts a court hearing in which food is the issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a board appointed to adjudicate on disputes.

clue.text: The German is digesting a hotel meal

indicators.note: is digesting means the German word swallows the hotel

parts.note: der is the German for 'the'
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A German man digests a hotel meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The German' is the German article DER, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is the main meal of the day.

clue.text: Licentious type reluctant to take a port

parts.note: loth means reluctant or unwilling
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A libertine is unwilling to drink a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' is Rio, a harbour city, not the wine; 'take' just joins LOTH to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, the seducer in Rowe's play 'The Fair Penitent', became the byword for a rake or womaniser.

clue.text: Game to provide cloaks for masquerades

definitions.meaning: a pastime played with spotted tiles
hooded cloaks with half-masks worn at masked balls

explanation.surface: A game supplies costumes for fancy-dress balls.
explanation.definitionFit: The tile game shares its name with the loose hooded cloak and mask worn at masquerades.

clue.text: Carver's vessel

explanation.definitionFit: One who cuts is a carver; a cutter is also a single-masted boat.
